v2_0_blockers.REPRODUCER: measured read-only 2026-10-05 03:30 (+07): ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db holds 14 sessions created 2026-10-04 17:53-23:13 local (titles 'developer S1', 'S1-dev', 'n'; directories under the tests' temporary out/work/ws), provider fakeprov, models model-1/m, 0 tokens, cost 0 — the windows in which workers J (execute ~17:53, session ~19:45-20:24), K3 (execute, 21:12-21:15) and K5 (execute and session, 22:09-23:13) and the controller's own scratch verification runs (verify2.py, execute, ~18:54-18:59) ran those targets' mutants; ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log over the same window: 14 runs, 60 LLM request attempts, every one to fakeprov/model-1 (endpoint https://provider.invalid/v1, a reserved name that never resolves, or no base URL), every one AI_APICallError 'Cannot connect to API'; no other host named; 2 runs read the operator's ~/.config/opencode configuration and made no request; 12 snapshot directories written under ~/.local/share/opencode/snapshot. The unmutated code never does this: the full local suite of 1ba5bde (02:52-03:33) created no session

risks_not_findings.what: G7 needs every LedgerLock story successful (§17). Attempts 3 and 4 — the same workload repository, plan and route — both ended 4/7 for one measured cause: the developer wrote a 4-field ('delete', key, rid, ts) record, contrary to requirement §5's (op, key, value, rid, ts), copied from the legacy _bmad-output/epics.md that the workload repository holds at the plan's baseline (61 files under _bmad-output/); STORY-03-01 and STORY-04-02 were refuted three times each and STORY-04-01 followed. Neither that context nor the refuting probe's missing diagnostic (PROBE-DIAGNOSTIC-GAP-001, V21-04) is changed by the release, so the one smoke is expected to fail the same way; the budget is secondary
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a release blocker under §1 (model/workload, not the shipped runtime); reported to the owner as a decision before S6: run as chartered, or rule a workload/context change before the preregistration

measured.reading: the 400,000 ceiling binds only when two or more stories need their third attempt; a run whose stories commit within two attempts stays near 250,000 by these per-session figures

risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: not reproduced; watched in the S2-exit full suite and the RC CI

risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: a fixture defect — git now writes the included file (`git config -f`), escaping the value; the old-git exposure it led to is B4-OLD-GIT

risks_not_findings.what: S2 mutation worker G (snapshot 369c8ac), target cli_invocation.py::_preflight: the unmutated kill tests (tests/v2/test_c2_cli_protocol.py, tests/v2/test_c2_cli_invocation.py) failed once (2026-10-04 ~14:52), so the runner refused the target ('kill tests fail on the unmutated tree (leaked 0)'). Seven other G targets with the same kill set passed that baseline; three faithful runs of both files on 369c8ac (the tree mutation.py builds), under the same load (workers G and I running), all passed (62 s / 66 s each). The runner keeps no test output, so the failing test is not known; a timing failure under load (cf. OBS-S2-1) is the remaining candidate.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: not reproduced. The errored result is kept in worker G's history and excluded by the qualifier ('the run errored'); _preflight is re-measured in the final round K

risks_not_findings.what: A second baseline failure of the same kill files: worker I (369c8ac), cli_invocation.py::AGENT/op_call (2026-10-04 ~16:05; the failed baseline ended ~95 s after the previous target, so a test failed early, not the 300 s runner timeout). Not reproduced: test_c2_cli_protocol.py + test_c2_cli_invocation.py 15/15 runs each on a faithful 369c8ac tree under the same load (OBS-S2-3's 3 plus 12 more), and the timing-tightest case (Harness.test_CLI_2b…, a 3 s harness watchdog) 20/20. Two of about 50 campaign baselines of these files failed; the runner discarded the kill tests' output, so the failing test is unknown. Consequence for the evidence: a spurious failure while measuring a mutant would count as a kill, so a survivor could be masked at about that rate; the mutants of these files' targets are otherwise killed by assertion.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding (not reproduced). validation/v2/mutation.py now keeps the failing kill-test file, exit status and output tail of a failing baseline in the result ('baseline'); both errored targets (_preflight, AGENT/op_call) are re-measured in round K with it

risks_not_findings.what: aisef2/app/run.py execute: the client lookup `shutil.which('opencode', path=client.environment(...).get('PATH'))` carried an equivalent mutant (S2 mutation, worker J: 'PATH' emptied survives): the client environment copies the operator's PATH verbatim, and shutil.which with path=None reads the same os.environ PATH, so no test can tell them apart; audits are not accepted for kernel targets (validation/qualification/q2.py).
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: the lookup now reads `.get('PATH', '')` — exactly the PATH the run gives the client; none given, nothing found (never os.defpath's fallback, which the client would not search either). The mutant is then killed (tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py AppExecute: the client found on the run's PATH). A second candidate, the `(out / 'repo').exists()` guard of final_main, was measured NOT equivalent (test_app_units' old-git test kills it: a refused run runs no git at all) and is unchanged.

risks_not_findings.what: aisef2/app/settings.py load: `sorted(pre) != ['chat_probes']` carried an equivalent mutant (S2 mutation, worker J2: 'L117 sorted() -> list()' survives): for a mapping, the sorted and the listed keys equal a one-element list together or not at all; audits are not accepted for kernel targets.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: written `set(pre) != {'chat_probes'}` — the same test of exactly that one key; its mutants are killed (the existing settings tests and tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py AppSettingsLoad)

risks_not_findings.what: aisef2/app/bundle.py load: `ContractApproval(**{**a, 'model_reviews': tuple(a['model_reviews'])})` carried two equivalent mutants (S2 mutation, worker J2: the override dropped, its tuple() -> list()): ContractApproval's own __post_init__ already makes model_reviews a tuple. The override also accepted a string, splitting 'abc' into ('a', 'b', 'c') review references.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: the override removed (`ContractApproval(**a)`); a non-list model_reviews is now refused as a bundle error (ContractError is a ValueError), pinned by tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py AppBundleLoad

risks_not_findings.what: aisef2/app/adapters.py Reviewer.review: `except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError)` around `json.loads(m.group(0))['findings']` carried an equivalent mutant (S2 mutation, worker J2: TypeError dropped survives): a {...} match loads as an object or raises ValueError, and indexing an object raises KeyError only.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: the unreachable TypeError removed from the clause; dropping either remaining element is killed by the existing review tests (invalid JSON, no findings key)

risks_not_findings.what: aisef2/app/preflight.py run: the observation's initial `"listing": None` placeholder carried an equivalent mutant (S2 mutation, worker J: 'L70 dict entry 4 dropped' survives): the entry is always overwritten before anything reads it, and the record is written with sorted keys.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: the placeholder removed (the listing is added once measured); every read of obs['listing'] follows that assignment

risks_not_findings.what: tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py ClientEnvironment (written for client.environment's survivors) put distinct values in SYSTEMROOT and SystemRoot; on Windows os.environ is case-insensitive, so the two are one variable and the case failed there (CI 37207425787, windows-latest 3.11; every other job only the three mutation-bound checks).
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: a test defect, the product is right; fixed 5025e56 (one value per name ignoring case; all 37 client.environment mutants still killed). The fix staled final round K at ba88eaa: the controller stopped handoff-K.sh before K4 started and K3 in its first target (no result; its log kept, K3.history.json); round K re-ran as K5/K6 at c6c3a55. CI on c6c3a55 (37210881575): all six unit jobs only the three mutation-bound checks.

risks_not_findings.what: Two kill cases first in their targets' kill sets stopped being first inside their file: unittest runs a module's classes in name order, and cases added later to tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py (AgentGuarded, AgentInvoke, AgentPlain before AgentSend; the session cases before ClientWaitWithin) reach the mutants first and wait until the runner's 300 s timeout — K5 measured AGENT/send L27 (newline emptied) and client.wait_within L153 ('And swapped') as killed only by the clock.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: tests/v2/test_s2_kills_k.py imports AgentSend and ClientWaitWithin and runs first in exactly those two kill sets (fc24d30); both mutants are killed at once by assertion; K7 re-measured the two targets.

risks_not_findings.what: bundle.Project.order L64 'sorted() -> list()' survived in K5 although J and J2 had killed it: without sorted() the stories run in a set's iteration order, which string hashing randomizes per process, so the existing cases killed it only when that order happened not to be name order. Two kills written earlier in the campaign have the same shape with fixed names — preflight.fingerprint_fields L116/L117 (AppPreflightFingerprint, six names) and client.Budget.spend L74 (ClientBudget) — and miss their mutant only when the hash order of their names equals name order (about 1 run in 720 for six names); round K (K6) measured both killed.
risks_not_findings.disposition: not a finding: tests/v2/test_s2_kills_k.py AppProjectOrder picks story names whose set order differs from name order in the running process, then asserts name order (deterministic; 6 runs under 6 hash seeds, killed by assertion each time); K7 re-measured Project.order. The two fixed-name kills are left as measured: making them deterministic means editing tests/v2/test_s2_kills.py, which would stale every round-K result.
